subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Types of Disabilities in Digital Context
description: A quick win: understand Types of Disabilities in Digital Context.

hook.text: A developer thinks accessibility means screen readers. That covers vision. What about hearing, motor, and cognition?

buildup.text: Visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive disabilities each create distinct barriers to digital content.

discovery.text: Temporary disabilities count too: a broken arm, an ear infection, or brain fog from medication.

twist.text: Situational barriers affect everyone: bright sun makes screens hard to see, loud rooms make audio useless.

climax.text: Designing for permanent, temporary, and situational disabilities creates products that work for all users.

punchline.text: Disability is a spectrum. Design for the spectrum.

quiz.question: What are situational disabilities?
options: Temporary barriers like bright sun or a noisy room
